schemaPath.description: Relative path to this file's schema; rewritten by the canonical writer.

identifier.description: A conceptual name: letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit.

label.description: A non-empty name of up to 256 characters without control characters.

tagLabel.description: A tag: a free-form label (SPEC section 5) of 1 to 64 characters without whitespace or control characters.

builtInVerb.description: A built-in verb (verbs-design.md decision 1): a fixed key whose meaning never changes. Made from the engine's table (Model/BuiltInVerbs.cs); a test checks they agree.

oneOf.title: Promote
oneOf.description: Move the object forward to a next state of its lifecycle.

oneOf.title: Demote
oneOf.description: Move the object back to an earlier state of its lifecycle.

oneOf.title: Override
oneOf.description: Make a move although its conditions or signatures are not met.

oneOf.title: Set state
oneOf.description: Put the object in a chosen state directly, without a declared move.

oneOf.title: Sign
oneOf.description: Give a signature that a move needs.

oneOf.title: Reject
oneOf.description: Refuse a signature, so the move does not happen.

oneOf.title: Ignore
oneOf.description: Waive a signature, so the move no longer waits for it.

oneOf.title: Withdraw
oneOf.description: Take back a signature already given.

oneOf.title: Delegate
oneOf.description: Hand a signature or a task to another actor.

oneOf.title: Route
oneOf.description: Send the object to actors for review, signature or a task.

oneOf.title: Claim
oneOf.description: Take a task offered to several actors, so only you hold it.

oneOf.title: Complete
oneOf.description: Finish a task.

oneOf.title: Create
oneOf.description: Make a new object.

oneOf.title: Read
oneOf.description: See an object or a link, and its data.

oneOf.title: Modify
oneOf.description: Change the values of an object or a link.

oneOf.title: Delete
oneOf.description: Remove an object.

oneOf.title: Copy
oneOf.description: Make a new object from an existing one.

oneOf.title: Revise
oneOf.description: Make the next revision of an object.

oneOf.title: Lock
oneOf.description: Reserve an object, so only the actor holding the lock may change it.

oneOf.title: Unlock
oneOf.description: Release a lock.

oneOf.title: Change owner
oneOf.description: Give an object another owner.

oneOf.title: Change type
oneOf.description: Make an object an instance of another type.

oneOf.title: Change lifecycle
oneOf.description: Put an object under another lifecycle.

oneOf.title: Freeze
oneOf.description: Make an object or a link read-only until it is thawed. While frozen it can't be modified, connected, disconnected or deleted.

oneOf.title: Thaw
oneOf.description: Undo a freeze.

oneOf.title: Connect
oneOf.description: Link two objects through a relation.

oneOf.title: Disconnect
oneOf.description: Remove a link between two objects.

verbRef.description: A verb, by key: a built-in verb, or one of the project's own verbs (model/vocabularies/verbs.json). A key neither declares is MQ9701.

description.description: Markdown text, or a sidecar Markdown file beside the element's file.

status.description: The status of an element or sub-element: proposed, approved, deprecated or retired. It has no default. A reference to a retired element warns (MQ2022).

suppressions.description: Findings the element accepts, each with the reason it is the exception (on the element's file only, never inside a part). A finding is suppressed when it is on the element (its file is the element's file), and on the member when member is set, and its rule is the entry's rule; the first matching entry wins. Suppressed findings leave the report's counts and are listed apart with their reason. MQ5018: a rule that cannot be suppressed; MQ5019: an unknown rule or member, or a repeated entry; MQ5020: an entry no finding matched in a whole-model validate.

rule.description: The rule whose findings the entry accepts: a built-in rule (MQ followed by four digits), a script rule or a declared rule (x/<id>).

member.description: Limits the entry to one part of the element: a part in its file (its id), an attribute it holds through a base or a stereotype (the attribute's id), or an inherited member (the keyed id, <table key>.<member id>). Omitted: the whole element.

reason.description: Why this element is the exception.

properties.description: Custom property values, validated by extension schemas.

xRef.description: The x-ref keyword of a custom property schema (an extension file's properties, a stereotype's parameters, a custom kind's properties, a pack's parameterSchema): the string it sits on, or each item of the array whose items it sits on, is the id of an element or sub-element. It goes on a schema of type string or on an array's items, under properties, items or additionalProperties only; anything else is MQ2009. Values are ids (or ids joined by '.', the keyed id of an inherited member): the index lists them as references, so where-used, delete refusals and remove-references see them.

kind.description: The kinds the value may name: element kind names (entity, table...), sub-element kinds as the index names them (attribute, enum-member, column, row, state...), member (a member of a custom element), custom (any custom element) or custom:<type> with a kebab-case type, which matches the custom elements of that type (none when the project declares no such custom kind, so a shared schema may name custom kinds a project lacks).

of.description: For sub-element kinds only: "$element" (a member of the element whose file holds the value, its base chain and its stereotypes included) or an element id (a row whose seed targets that element; with kind member, a member of that custom element).

sameDatabase.description: For physical kinds only: the target must be in the database of the element holding the value.

optional.description: Whether a delete with remove-references may clear the value; a required one refuses it.

generation.description: Per-pack generation hints; the key is a pack name or "*".

extensions.description: Opaque data an import kept (unknown source configuration, by JSON pointer), written back on export.

columnType.description: A column's type keyword: a built-in scalar type, or range or multirange (PostgreSQL's built-in range types, with a subtype; multirange needs PostgreSQL 14 or later). Elsewhere a range column is stored as the dialect's text type (MQ4056).

rangeSubtype.description: The type of a range or multirange column's bounds: one of the keywords PostgreSQL has a built-in range for (int4range, int8range, numrange, daterange, tsrange, tstzrange).

typeRef.description: A built-in keyword, or a reference to an enum, value object, custom scalar type or reference type.

columnTypeRef.description: The logical type of a column: an enum, a reference type or a scalar type, beside the column's physical type keyword.

sensitivity.description: Whether a value is personal data (pii) or a secret.

dbTypeRef.description: A built-in type keyword, or the id of a database type of the same database (routine parameters and results, composite type fields).

storageChoice.description: A storage choice for reference data: a strategy key the project declares in referenceData.strategies (absent means template-defined) and its options.

storage.description: Storage parameters per dialect name (postgresql, sqlserver, mysql, oracle): each a map of parameter name to value, written in the DDL of a database of that dialect only (PostgreSQL and SQL Server WITH (name = value), MySQL table options, Oracle physical attributes). A number or boolean is written as the dialect writes it; a string is written as SQL as it is.

dialectMap.description: Dialect name (postgresql, sqlserver, mysql, sqlite, oracle) or "*" to SQL text.

derived.description: How a derived attribute is computed: by raw text (expression) or by an expression tree (value), exactly one of the two (MQ3107).

expression.description: The raw expression, interpreted by templates.

value.description: The value as an expression of the attribute's type.

rationale.description: Markdown text: why the element is shaped this way.

decision.description: A URL or a reference (such as ADR-0042) of the decision record. It is not an element id and is not checked.

attribute.description: Overlay: the synthesized column key this column overrides.

typeRef.description: Designed, imported, extra and contributed columns: the enum, reference type or scalar type whose values the column holds. Not on an overlay entry of a projected column, whose attribute types it, nor on a column a reference type's binding fills with a field (MQ4082).

subtype.description: The bound type of a range or multirange column, and only of one (MQ4057). A range column takes no length, precision or scale (MQ3013).

unicode.description: String and text columns: true stores Unicode text (SQL Server nvarchar and nchar, Oracle nvarchar2 and nchar, MySQL the utf8mb4 character set), false single-byte text (SQL Server varchar and char, Oracle varchar2 and char); absent takes the dialect's default, which is Unicode on SQL Server. PostgreSQL and SQLite keep every text in the database's encoding, so it changes nothing there. The type map's string:unicode, string:ansi and text:unicode entries decide the native types.

fixedLength.description: String and binary columns: a fixed-length type of the column's length (char, nchar, binary) instead of a varying one; the type map's string:fixed and binary:fixed entries decide the native types.

nullable.description: Designed or extra column: true (the default) or false. Overlay (with attribute): omitted keeps the synthesized value.

defaultName.description: The name of the column's default constraint, where the dialect names defaults (SQL Server); absent names it df_<table>_<column>. Other dialects keep defaults in the column and ignore it.

identity.description: With generated identity: the identity's first value (seed), its step (increment) and whether the database always generates the value and refuses one an insert gives (always, GENERATED ALWAYS) instead of generating it only when none is given (GENERATED BY DEFAULT). PostgreSQL and Oracle write all three; SQL Server writes IDENTITY(seed, increment) and always generates; MySQL writes the seed as the table's AUTO_INCREMENT; what a dialect lacks is left out (MQ4056).

stableId.description: A uuid column the database does not fill (no identity, sequence, generation or computation; MQ7124): every row a database receives into the table gets a stable id there, RFC 9562 UUID version 5 with the table id as namespace and the row key's values as name, unless the row's source writes the column (a binding's field or constant). The row key may hold neither this column nor a value the database fills (MQ7125). A table seed gives no cell for it (MQ7108).

sensitive.description: Whether the column holds personal data or a secret. An overlay entry states it for its projected column.

rationale.description: Markdown text: why the element is shaped this way.

decision.description: A URL or a reference (such as ADR-0042) of the decision record. It is not an element id and is not checked.

id.description: The key's id. Optional on a table; a key with an id is a sub-element that other elements can name.

withoutOverlaps.description: Whether the key's last column is a period (a range or multirange column) that may repeat a value of the other columns as long as the periods do not overlap: a temporal key (WITHOUT OVERLAPS, PostgreSQL 18 and later; MQ4056 elsewhere). Needs a column before it, and the btree_gist extension for its other columns.

nullsNotDistinct.description: Whether two rows with nulls in the columns conflict (NULLS NOT DISTINCT, PostgreSQL 15 and later); the other dialects leave it out (MQ4056).

withoutOverlaps.description: Whether the key's last column is a period (a range or multirange column) that may repeat a value of the other columns as long as the periods do not overlap: a temporal key (WITHOUT OVERLAPS, PostgreSQL 18 and later; MQ4056 elsewhere). Needs a column before it, and the btree_gist extension for its other columns.

period.description: Whether the last column pair is a period (PERIOD): each referencing row's period must be covered by referenced rows' periods, which a temporal key (withoutOverlaps) of the referenced table holds. PostgreSQL 18 and later; MQ4056 elsewhere.

onDeleteColumns.description: With onDelete set-null or set-default: the key's columns the action sets, a subset of columns (ON DELETE SET NULL (column, ...)). Empty sets every column of the key. Only PostgreSQL has a column list (MQ4056); on the other dialects the action sets every column.

deferrable.description: When the key is checked: not-deferrable (every statement), initially-immediate (every statement unless a transaction defers it with SET CONSTRAINTS) or initially-deferred (at commit). PostgreSQL, SQLite and Oracle have deferrable keys; SQL Server and MySQL check every statement and leave it out (MQ4056).

checkConstraint.title: Check constraint
checkConstraint.description: A check: SQL text per dialect (expression) or an expression tree (condition), exactly one of the two (MQ3107).

column.description: A column check: the id or key of the column it constrains. The constraint is written in the table like any other check; a migration that drops the column drops the check first.

condition.description: The condition as an expression tree over the table's columns; unknown passes, as in any CHECK.

properties.description: Custom property values, for a schema that applies to the kind check. They reach templates only, never the check's DDL.

entityCheck.title: Entity check
entityCheck.description: A condition every record of the entity meets; unknown passes, as in a CHECK. A database enforces it only through a binding that lists it in checks.

attribute.description: The attribute a failure points at: an id, or the keyed id of an inherited or contributed attribute (MQ3114 when the condition does not read it).

condition.description: The condition, a boolean expression over the entity's own attributes.

rationale.description: Markdown text: why the element is shaped this way.

decision.description: A URL or a reference (such as ADR-0042) of the decision record. It is not an element id and is not checked.

expr.title: Expression
expr.description: A node of the one expression language. Exactly one of: value (with type for a literal written as text), null, path (ids; with old, the values before the verb, at trigger point sites only), ref (an enum member or reference-type code id), member (rule conditions only), now (guard, set, right and trigger point sites only), currentActor (guard, set, right and trigger point sites only), inState (with of; guard, set, right and trigger point sites only), op with args, call with args, case (with else), satisfies with with, text (accepted on writes and stored as a tree; in a file it is MQ3108).

value.description: A literal: a string, an integer or a boolean; with type, the value's text, so that digits are kept.

type.description: The type of a literal written as text.

path.description: To-one navigation ids (relation end ids), then one attribute, column, input member, context or payload attribute, or constraint parameter id; attributeId.memberId for a value object member; keyed ids for inherited and contributed members.

old.description: With path: the path reads the object's values before the verb (old.price in text), null on create. Trigger point sites only (when, condition and set values); elsewhere it is MQ3104.

ref.description: The id of an enum member or of a reference-type code.

member.description: A member of the selected object in the path syntax of declared rules (properties.retentionDays); rule conditions only.

now.description: The clock, a datetimeoffset; guard, set, right and trigger point sites only.

currentActor.description: The identity of whoever acts: the step's signer, else its participant's identity or name, else the name of the actor it acts as, else null. It takes the type of what it meets (a comparison, in, coalesce, a case branch, a set's attribute), else it is a string; guard, set, right and trigger point sites only.

inState.description: True when the object is in any of these states of one lifecycle (state ids); a compound state counts when any state inside it is active. Guard, set, right and trigger point sites only.

of.description: The to-one relation end ids from the subject to the object whose state inState reads; absent, the subject itself. Only with inState.

call.description: A function of the closed table (trim, length, matches, nonnull_count, add_days, add_months, date_part, date_of, round, json_type, json_length); another name is MQ3101.

satisfies.description: The id of the constraint cited.

with.description: One argument per parameter of the constraint.

text.description: The expression as text, parsed in the site's scope.

parameter.description: The id of the constraint's parameter.

expression.description: An expression indexed instead of a column (a functional index), per dialect name or "*": written in parentheses. A dialect without an entry leaves the index out; SQL Server indexes no expression (MQ4056: index a computed column instead), MySQL from 8.0.13 (not MariaDB).

operatorClass.description: The operator class the column or expression is indexed with (PostgreSQL), such as gin_trgm_ops for a trigram index or vector_cosine_ops for a vector index; written after it as it is, so it may carry parameters (gist_trgm_ops (siglen = 32)). MQ4056 elsewhere.

nulls.description: Where nulls sort: PostgreSQL's NULLS FIRST or NULLS LAST. Unset keeps the direction's default (last ascending, first descending), and a value equal to it changes nothing. MQ4056 elsewhere.

length.description: A key prefix length: only the first characters or bytes of the column are indexed (MySQL, which needs one for a text or blob column; the other dialects leave it out, MQ4056).

method.description: The index method: btree and hash (PostgreSQL, MySQL); gin, gist, spgist and brin (PostgreSQL); hnsw and ivfflat (PostgreSQL with the vector extension, which a SQL object with phase before creates); clustered (SQL Server, and PostgreSQL CLUSTER). MQ4056 where the dialect lacks it.

storage.description: Index storage parameters per dialect (PostgreSQL and SQL Server WITH (...), such as fillfactor, pages_per_range for brin, m and ef_construction for hnsw, lists for ivfflat). MySQL and Oracle leave them out (MQ4056).

operationError.title: Operation error
operationError.description: An error an operation can report. Its display name and description are the texts a client shows.

code.description: The stable text clients see; absent, the name.

input.description: The input member the error points at, one of the operation's own (MQ3027).

rationale.description: Markdown text: why the element is shaped this way.

decision.description: A URL or a reference (such as ADR-0042) of the decision record. It is not an element id and is not checked.

rightBody.title: Right body
rightBody.description: What a right says (rights-design.md decisions 3 to 6), shared by an inline right in a lifecycle's rights and a named right (model/rights/): it allows or denies some actors some verbs, under an optional condition. Each form refers to these properties one by one.

access.description: allow or deny. Each lifecycle that answers says no when a deny that holds names the verb, else yes when an allow holds, else its rightsDefault answers; one no decides.

actors.description: Who the right applies to: any actor, as an event's actors (people, roles, groups, organizations, external systems, the system actor, actors from the object). A role, group or organization stands for its members at any depth. Empty means everyone.

except.description: Actors the right does not apply to, with their members at any depth; other rights and the lifecycle's default still answer for them, so it never grants. An entry that actors also names is MQ9906.

verbs.description: What the right speaks of, at least one verb: a built-in verb's key or one of the project's own (MQ9701). A move, signature or task verb speaks of this lifecycle's moves, signatures and human tasks; an object, link or own verb speaks of the object, whichever lifecycle acts.

ends.description: Relation ends of the subject: the right then speaks of the links through them, for connect, disconnect, read, modify, freeze and thaw. Ends every subject holds, beside only those verbs (MQ9903).

attributes.description: Attributes of the subject: the right then speaks of reading or modifying only those. Attributes every subject holds, beside only read and modify (MQ9903). A modify that changes several attributes is checked per attribute against the rights that name attributes, and one no refuses it; a right without attributes is checked once, as before.

whileFrozen.description: true: the right holds only while the object is frozen, or with ends, while the link is. Freezing itself refuses modify, connect, disconnect and delete; a whileFrozen right adds any other verb, such as change-owner or one of the project's own.

condition.description: The right holds only when this is true; false or unknown means it says nothing. It reads the object under subject (to-one paths too), current_actor(), in_state and now(), not the context or a payload.

triggerBody.title: Trigger point body
triggerBody.description: What a trigger point says (trigger-points-design.md decisions 3 to 12), shared by an entry of a lifecycle's triggerPoints and a named trigger point (model/trigger-points/): what runs when one of its verbs happens, and where. A check has a condition, an action or a replace has sets; with neither, the body is the team's code. Each form refers to these properties one by one.

type.description: check: judges the change and passes, warns or refuses with its message. action: does something at its timing. replace: takes the place of the verb's built-in effect, only on delete, disconnect, copy and revise (MQ8103); everything around it still runs.

timing.description: An action's moment, required on an action and allowed nowhere else (MQ8101). before: fills the proposed values before the checks, and nothing is written until they pass. with-change: after the effect, in the same unit of work, so a failure undoes the verb. after-commit: once the change is saved; it cannot undo it, may run late and may run more than once, and sets nothing (MQ8105).

severity.description: A check's severity, allowed only on a check (MQ8101). error (also when absent) refuses the step with refusal check; warning lets it through and lists the check in the trace's checkWarnings.

verbs.description: The verbs it runs on, at least one: a built-in verb's key or one of the project's own (MQ9701). A move, signature or task verb runs in this lifecycle's moves, signatures and human tasks; an object, link or own verb runs on the object, whichever lifecycle acts.

entities.description: Entities it runs for, each with its derived entities: some of those its lifecycle governs (MQ8102). Empty: every entity its subjects cover. It also widens what its paths and sets may name to what every entity it covers holds under one id.

attributes.description: Attributes of the subject: it runs only when a read or modify step itself reads or changes one of them, beside only read and modify and never beside ends (MQ8102). When a step does not say which, a check runs and an action or a replace does not, and a note says so.

ends.description: Relation ends of the subject: it runs only for the links through them, for connect, disconnect, read, modify, freeze and thaw (MQ8102). When a step does not say which, a check runs and an action or a replace does not, and a note says so.

when.description: It runs only when this is true; false or unknown skips it, and the trace says so. It reads the object under subject (the proposed values before the effect), its values before the verb under old, current_actor(), in_state and now(), not the context; a move's payload only as the payload rules allow (MQ3102).

condition.description: A check's condition: only true passes. It reads what when reads. Not on an action or a replace (MQ8101); without it, the check is the team's code, and a scenario step assumes its outcome.

sets.description: What an action or a replace sets on the object, as an action's sets: every value is worked out first, then all are applied. A value reads what when reads. Not on a check (MQ8101) or an after-commit action (MQ8105); without it, an action or a replace is the team's code.

outside.description: true: the team's code reaches outside systems. Simulation never runs the team's code; the trace marks the point, and generated tests record it instead of calling it. Only a point with team code may say so (MQ8101); a with-change one is warned (MQ8106).

noBypass.description: true: no bulk load ever skips the trigger point. A bulk load skips the others only where the running system's host permits it; who may is the host's permission, not the model's. Simulation never skips any.
